original_value: Domain shift refers to the well known problem that a model trained in one source domain performs poorly when appliedto a target domain with different statistics. Domain Generalization (DG) techniques attempt to alleviate this issue by producing models which by design generalize well to novel testing domains. We propose a novel meta-learning method for domain generalization. Rather than designing a specific model that is robust to domain shift as in most previous DG work, we propose a model agnostic training procedure for DG. Our algorithm simulates train/test domain shift during training by synthesizing virtual testing domains within each mini-batch. The meta-optimization objective requires that steps to improve training domain performance should also improve testing domain performance. This meta-learning procedure trains models with good generalization ability to novel domains. We evaluate our method and achieve state of the art results on a recent cross-domain image classification benchmark, as well demonstrating its potential on two classic reinforcement learning tasks.

result.paraphrase: Domain shift is the well-known issue where a model trained in one source domain performs poorly when applied to a target domain with different statistics. Domain Generalization (DG) methods try to reduce this problem by producing models that are, by design, able to generalize well to unseen test domains. We introduce a new meta-learning approach for domain generalization. Instead of crafting a particular model robust to domain shift, as in most prior DG work, we use a model-agnostic training procedure for DG. During training, our algorithm imitates train/test domain shift by generating virtual test domains inside each mini-batch. The meta-optimization objective demands that updates that improve training-domain performance also improve testing-domain performance. This meta-learning process trains models with strong generalization to new domains. We evaluate the method and obtain state-of-the-art results on a recent cross-domain image classification benchmark, while also showing its potential on two classic reinforcement learning tasks.
